NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)
The intervention is to incorporate a hydrophobic nano-clay reinforcement into the ethylene-vinyl alcohol (EVOH) layer to reduce moisture plasticization while maintaining barrier properties. Standard practice uses pure EVOH or blends with other polymers, which still allow moisture absorption and plasticization. This is a departure because the nano-clay creates a tortuous path for moisture molecules while the hydrophobic surface repels water, reducing plasticization without compromising the oxygen barrier. The closest existing practice is nanocomposite packaging in other industries (e.g., fuel tanks), but those use hydrophilic clays for mechanical reinforcement, not hydrophobic clays for moisture resistance.

PHYSICS CHECK
The governing relation is Fick's first law of diffusion: J = -D·(Δc/Δx), where J is flux, D is diffusivity, and Δc/Δx is concentration gradient. Nano-clay reduces D by increasing diffusion path length (tortuosity) and hydrophobic treatment lowers moisture solubility in the matrix. A 5% loading of montmorillonite clay with hydrophobic modification (e.g., quaternary ammonium treatment) can reduce moisture diffusivity by 40-60% in polymer matrices, while maintaining oxygen barrier properties by minimizing clay dispersion at <10nm to prevent light scattering.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
Standard Practice Bill:
- EVOH resin (procured)
- Adhesive layers (procured)
- Outer protective layer (e.g., polyethylene, procured)
- Co-extrusion equipment (existing)
- Quality control testing equipment (existing)

Intervention Bill:
- (b) Hydrophobic nano-clay (montmorillonite modified with quaternary ammonium salt, standard catalog item)
- (c) EVOH resin formulation procedure change (add 5% nano-clay by weight during masterbatch preparation)
- (a) Existing co-extrusion equipment (no change)
- (c) Quality control testing procedure update (add nano-clay dispersion verification via TEM sampling)
- (a) Existing adhesive layers (no change)
- (a) Existing outer protective layer (no change)

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
- Material cost: +3% for nano-clay additive (within procurement class, standard pricing)
- Processing: No change to co-extrusion equipment (class a)
- Quality control: Additional TEM sampling procedure (class c, within existing QC infrastructure)
- Labor: Minimal increase for masterbatch preparation (within operator skill class)
- Overall burden: Same class (minor material cost increase offset by no equipment changes)

EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol: Accelerated aging test at 40°C/75% RH for 6 months (equivalent to 18 months at 25°C/65% RH). Sample groups: (1) Standard EVOH packaging, (2) Nano-clay reinforced EVOH packaging (5% loading). Test water vapor transmission rate (WVTR) monthly using ASTM E96 gravimetric method. Instruments: Environmental chamber, analytical balance, test cups. Pass/fail: WVTR must remain <0.5 g/m2/day at all measurement points. Kill criterion: If any sample exceeds 0.5 g/m2/day at any point, the intervention fails. Duration: 6 months with monthly measurements.
